newsitem.title: USA: NYS Comptroller says NYC mayor disrupted audits.
newsitem.headline: NYS Comptroller says NYC mayor disrupted audits.

text.p: New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall said Tuesday that New York City Mayor Rudolph Guiliani's move to block certain city agency audits has, in turn, disrupted a several audits, some outside the city.
In a press briefing at his office at 270 Broadway here, McCall also said that more audits of city agencies are likely.

"There are several other audits that have been disrupted, and additional subpoenas will likely be issued," McCall said, in prepared remarks, explaining that some of the audits were part of statewide programs.

A deal between the state comptroller, a Democrat and a potential candidate for governor, and the Giuliani Administration, which evicted state auditors from city agencies because it viewed some audits as politically motivated, broke down on Monday.
A spokesman for Giuliani was not immediately available.
McCall said that using the powers of his office to issue audits was an unprecedented step during the four years that he has been state comptroller.
He also said the audits were objective and pointedly asked why the mayor, a Republican, had blocked them.

"It suggests he has something to hide, something he does not want to be discovered and disclosed to taxpayers," McCall said. He added he hoped the Giuliani Administration, which would have to go to court to overturn the subpoenas, now would let the state auditors continue their work.
The audits that the comptroller issued subpoenas for covered Police Department crime statistics.
Giuliani faces election in November and one of the hallmarks of his tenure has been a big drop in crime.

Other subpoenas covered: the security of vital records from the Department of Health, the Human Resources Administration's workfare plan, and the Department of Finance, to examine controls and tax breaks given to developers.
About eight audits were blocked by the Giuliani Administration, though some partly overlap with the ones for which the subpoenas were issued.
